question: Suppose $P$ is a $3 \times 3$ non-singular matrix such that $\text{adj} (P) = 2P$. What is $|P|$?
explanation:
Recall, for $n \times n$ matrix:
$\text{adj}(P) = |P| P^{-1}$
Given $\text{adj}(P) = 2P$.
Equate:
$|P| P^{-1} = 2P$
$\Rightarrow |P| I = 2P^2$
So $P^2 = \frac{1}{2}|P| I$.
Take determinants:
$|P^2| = \left| \frac{1}{2}|P| I \right|$
$|P|^2 = \left( \frac{1}{2}|P| \right)^3$
$|P|^2 = \frac{1}{8}|P|^3$
$|P|^3 - 8|P|^2 = 0$
$|P|^2 (|P| - 8) = 0$
$|P| = 0$ or $|P| = 8$.
But $P$ is non-singular, so $|P| \ne 0$.
Thus $|P| = 8$.
